senses.gloss: To force people to leave the home or the country where they have settled.
senses.ru: срывать с насиженного места, вынуждать покинуть дом
examples: The war *uprooted* thousands of families in a single week.
A transfer would *uproot* the whole family again.
They have been *uprooted* twice in five years.

senses.gloss: For a court, to cancel a ruling or a sentence so that it no longer stands.
examples: The appeals court *vacated* his conviction.
A judge can *vacate* the order if new evidence turns up.
The fine was *vacated* after the officer failed to appear.

senses.gloss: To show someone that their feelings or their experience are reasonable and worth taking seriously.
examples: A good friend will *validate* your feelings instead of arguing with them.
Her therapist *validated* what she had been going through for years.
He just wanted to feel *validated*, not fixed.

senses.gloss: To stamp or mark a parking ticket so that the customer pays less or nothing.
examples: Does the restaurant *validate* parking?
The front desk *validated* our ticket, so the garage was free.
Bring your stub to the counter to have it *validated*.

senses.gloss: To judge how much money something is worth.
examples: An expert will *value* the painting before the auction.
The insurance company *valued* the ring at four thousand dollars.
The house has been *valued* twice this year.

senses.gloss: To hide something so that it cannot be clearly seen or understood.
examples: Fog *veiled* the top of the bridge all morning.
The company *veils* its finances behind vague language.
It was a thinly *veiled* threat.

senses.gloss: To express anger or frustration freely, usually by talking about it.
senses.ru: выплёскивать эмоции, изливать (гнев), давать волю чувствам
examples: I just need to *vent* for a minute.
She *vented* her frustration to her sister on the phone.
He has been *venting* about his manager all week.

senses.gloss: To think of someone or something in a particular way.
examples: Many voters *view* the plan as a tax increase.
She *viewed* the offer with suspicion.
The move is widely *viewed* as a mistake.

senses.gloss: To intrude on someone's privacy or body, or on a place people treat as sacred.
examples: Searching her phone would *violate* her privacy.
Vandals *violated* several graves in the old cemetery.
She felt *violated* for weeks after the break-in.

senses.gloss: To give information that nobody has asked you for.
senses.ru: сообщать по собственной инициативе, вызваться сказать
examples: Don't *volunteer* anything the officer hasn't asked about.
He *volunteered* that he had been in the building that night.
Nobody has *volunteered* an explanation yet.

senses.gloss: To serve food and drinks to customers in a restaurant.
examples: He *waits* tables three nights a week.
She *waited* tables all through college.
I have *waited* tables at two different diners.

senses.gloss: To take a person or an animal somewhere on foot, going along with them.
examples: I *walk* the dog before breakfast every day.
He *walked* her home after the movie.
Our neighbor has been *walking* the puppy while we're at work.

senses.gloss: To let yourself sink into a sad or self-pitying feeling instead of moving past it.
examples: You can *wallow* for one more day, then get back to work.
He *wallowed* in self-pity for a month after the breakup.
She has been *wallowing* ever since the news came.

senses.gloss: To move somewhere in a casual, over-confident way that annoys other people.
examples: You can't just *waltz* past security like that.
He *waltzed* into the meeting twenty minutes late.
She came *waltzing* through the door as if nothing had happened.

senses.gloss: For your mind or your attention to drift away from what you should be thinking about.
examples: My mind *wanders* whenever a meeting runs long.
His attention *wandered* halfway through the lecture.
I caught my thoughts *wandering* again.

senses.gloss: To damage the way a person thinks or judges, making it unfair or unhealthy.
examples: Fame can *warp* a person's sense of what is normal.
Those years in prison *warped* his view of people.
He has a *warped* sense of humor.

senses.gloss: For moving water to carry something to a place.
senses.ru: выносить (водой), прибивать к берегу; смывать, смыть
examples: Bottles and driftwood *wash* onto this beach after every storm.
The flood *washed* topsoil into the creek.
A dead whale had *washed* ashore overnight.

senses.gloss: To look after a person, an animal, or someone's things for a short time.
examples: Could you *watch* my bag for a second?
Her mother *watched* the kids while she was at work.
We have been *watching* their cat all week.

senses.gloss: To be careful about something because it could cause trouble.
senses.ru: следить за, остерегаться; быть осторожным с
examples: *Watch* your step — those boards are loose.
He *watched* his language around the children.
I'm *watching* my salt these days.

senses.gloss: For the eyes to fill with tears, or for the mouth to fill with saliva.
examples: Onions make my eyes *water*.
His eyes *watered* in the cold wind.
The smell from the bakery had my mouth *watering*.

senses.gloss: To move your hand to signal to someone where to go or what to do.
senses.ru: показывать жестом, махнуть (направляя); подавать знак рукой
examples: Just *wave* the next car forward.
A guard *waved* us toward the side entrance.
The officer was *waving* traffic past the accident.

senses.gloss: For a flag or something light to move back and forth in the wind.
examples: Flags *wave* over the courthouse on holidays.
The wheat *waved* in the breeze.
A banner was *waving* from the balcony.

senses.gloss: To have a particular weight, or to measure how heavy something is.
examples: The package *weighs* about two pounds.
The nurse *weighed* the baby at every visit.
Have the bags been *weighed* yet?

senses.gloss: To be glad that something has happened and to say so.
examples: We *welcome* any feedback from customers.
Teachers *welcomed* the change to the schedule.
The ruling has been *welcomed* by both parties.

senses.gloss: For an animal or a machine to make a long, high, unhappy sound.
examples: The dog *whines* whenever we leave the house.
The engine *whined* as the truck climbed the hill.
Something under the hood has been *whining* since Tuesday.

senses.gloss: To strike a person or an animal with a whip, or to lash at something the way a whip does.
examples: He would never *whip* a horse to make it run faster.
The rider *whipped* the horse's flank.
Rain was *whipping* against the windows all night.

senses.gloss: To take someone or something somewhere very quickly.
examples: A car will *whisk* you from the airport to the hotel.
Guards *whisked* the senator into a waiting van.
She was *whisked* to the hospital in an ambulance.

senses.gloss: To erase everything stored on a phone, a drive, or a computer.
examples: Remember to *wipe* the phone before you sell it.
The update *wiped* all my saved photos.
The laptop had already been *wiped* when police got it.

senses.gloss: To send money electronically from one bank account to another.
examples: I can *wire* you the deposit today.
They *wired* the money on Friday afternoon.
The funds were *wired* to the wrong account.

senses.gloss: To say that you hope someone will have something good.
examples: Everyone stopped by to *wish* her luck.
He *wished* us a safe trip.
I have already *wished* him a happy birthday.

senses.gloss: To sign a document to confirm that you saw someone else sign it.
examples: Two people must *witness* the signature.
A notary *witnessed* the will.
The contract was *witnessed* by her lawyer.

senses.gloss: For a machine, a system, or a plan to do what it is supposed to do.
examples: The elevator doesn't *work* again.
The medicine *worked* within an hour.
Their plan has *worked* better than anyone expected.

senses.gloss: To operate a machine or a piece of equipment.
senses.ru: управлять (механизмом), уметь обращаться с, работать на (станке)
examples: Can you *work* the projector?
She *worked* the register while the manager was out.
He has been *working* that crane for twenty years.

senses.gloss: To make someone feel anxious.
examples: It *worries* me that she hasn't called.
The test results *worried* his doctor.
You're *worrying* your mother.

senses.gloss: To honor a god, especially by taking part in a religious service.
examples: The family *worships* at a small church downtown.
They *worshiped* in secret for years.
People have *worshiped* at this spring for centuries.

senses.gloss: To hurt someone's feelings deeply.
examples: That remark *wounded* her more than he realized.
Criticism like that can *wound* a young writer.
He looked genuinely *wounded* by the question.

senses.gloss: To produce a result, a crop, or an amount of money.
examples: These bonds *yield* about four percent.
The search *yielded* nothing useful.
Those two acres have *yielded* more corn than the rest of the farm.

senses.gloss: To stop resisting and give in to pressure or force.
examples: He refused to *yield* to the pressure.
The old door *yielded* after a hard shove.
The company has *yielded* on almost every demand.

senses.gloss: To move very fast.
examples: Cars *zip* down this street all night.
A bike *zipped* past me on the sidewalk.
We were *zipping* along at eighty.

senses.gloss: To compress computer files into one smaller package.
examples: Please *zip* the folder before you email it.
I *zipped* the photos into a single file.
The files were *zipped* and sent overnight.

senses.gloss: To move very fast with a loud rushing sound.
examples: Motorcycles *zoom* past the house all summer.
A truck *zoomed* by and soaked us.
The kids were *zooming* around the yard on scooters.
